lesson_title: A Wallet, a Street and a Vetkoek Stand
hook_text: R350 in the wallet. R580 on the fridge list. Congratulations — you already understand economics.
clip_script: Month-end in the kitchen. The wallet holds three hundred and fifty rand; the list on the fridge adds up to five hundred and eighty. Nobody did anything wrong — that gap is just how economic life is, in every household and every treasury on earth. And every choice has a hidden second price: buy the soccer boots, and the real cost is the best thing that money would otherwise have done. Now follow the money. Saturday morning, one main road: the fish shop pays wages, the wages cross to the hardware store and the salon, the takings pay wages again — money running a relay in a circle, with leaks that drain it and refills that keep it spinning. And at the school gate, a vetkoek stand settles the oldest argument in the world: fifteen rand and the tray is still full at ten o'clock; three rand and it's empty before assembly; near seven rand, the last vetkoek meets the last hungry learner and nobody needed a meeting. Scarcity. The circular flow. Equilibrium. Half a year of economics, and it was standing in your kitchen the whole time.
visual_style: A fridge list growing longer beside a thin wallet; coins racing a relay loop around hand-drawn shopfronts with leak-drips and refill-taps; a vetkoek tray whose price tag flips as a queue forms and dissolves.
mood: Warm, familiar, quietly eye-opening — the everyday revealed as machinery.
pacing: Settled open in the kitchen, rolling momentum around the street, quick playful beats at the stand, assured close.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep and carry the half-year into your exam as four structures.
